questions.question: The interior plateau of South Africa is best described as:
options: A high, ancient erosion surface mostly between 1 200 and 1 800 metres, carrying the Highveld, Free State plains and Karoo basin

questions.question: The Great Escarpment is:
options: A river valley crossing the plateau
The nearly continuous rim where the plateau breaks off toward the sea, at its highest in the Drakensberg above 3 000 metres
The flat centre of the Karoo
A beach terrace along the coast

questions.question: The marginal zone between escarpment and sea includes:
options: The folded Cape ranges, stepped terrace country and the humid east-coast lowlands

questions.question: A convex slope differs from a concave slope because the convex slope:
options: Holds one constant angle like a ruler
Is gentlest at the top and steepest in the middle only
BULGES outward and steepens downhill, while the concave slope hollows inward and is gentlest at its base

questions.question: From summit to plain, the four slope elements run:
The cliff is called the FREE FACE because:
options: It is free of any rock
Rock freed from it by weathering falls away at once instead of lying where it loosened, keeping the face sheer
It faces away from the sun

questions.question: The talus slope is rectilinear because:
options: Loose fragments settle at their ANGLE OF REPOSE, roughly 25 to 35 degrees — the steepest angle at which they can rest

questions.question: The pediment at the slope's base is:
options: A gently CONCAVE surface under about 5 degrees, cut across bedrock with a thin sediment veneer, merging with the plain

subtopics.title: Slope Retreat — How the Profile Moves

questions.question: In parallel slope retreat, the profile:
options: Keeps its PROPORTIONS — cliff steep, talus at repose, pediment gentle — while the whole staircase relocates backward
Flattens and rounds until the cliff vanishes
Stays fixed in one place forever

questions.question: As opposing slopes retreat over deep time:
options: Pediments from neighbouring valleys meet and merge into a PEDIPLAIN, leaving koppies and inselbergs as survivors

questions.question: The rival model of slope DECLINE describes:
options: Slopes moving backward at constant angle
The whole profile lowering and rounding with age — typical of humid regions with deep soils and thick vegetation

questions.question: South African conditions favour parallel retreat because of:
options: Heavy year-round rainfall and deep soils
The absence of any hard rock
Semi-arid climate, resistant caprocks and sparse vegetation — which keep profiles sharp for tens of millions of years

subtopics.title: GIS — Resolution, Data Types, Raster and Vector

questions.question: Spatial resolution is:
options: The ground size represented by one pixel — at 30 metres a school registers but a minibus vanishes
The number of wavelength bands a sensor records
The number of layers in a GIS

questions.question: High spectral resolution helps analysts because:
options: More, narrower wavelength bands let different surfaces — stressed crops, healthy veld, bare soil, water — be told apart by their reflectance signatures
It removes clouds from the image
It converts raster to vector automatically

questions.question: In vector data, a windpump, a river and a farm are stored respectively as:
options: POINT, LINE and AREA — each with its own table of attribute facts

questions.question: Raster data suits altitude and rainfall because:
options: They are discrete objects with sharp edges
They vary CONTINUOUSLY across the land, which a grid of cells each holding one value captures naturally

subtopics.title: The Country Is a Wedding Cake

questions.question: In the wedding-cake picture, the cake top, cake side and table stand for:
options: The interior plateau, the Great Escarpment and the marginal zone

questions.question: Rivers leaving the top of the cake must jump the side, which is why:
options: All South African rivers flow inland
The Tugela plunges nearly 950 metres off the Drakensberg rim in one of the world's tallest falls
There are no waterfalls in South Africa
The rivers stop at the escarpment

questions.question: The rugby ball, the skateboard ramp and the ruler stand for:
options: CONVEX, CONCAVE and RECTILINEAR slope shapes

questions.question: In the stadium picture, roof, wall, stands and pitch stand for:
The stands always sit at the same steepness because:
options: Loose rock settles at its ANGLE OF REPOSE, about 25 to 35 degrees — overload it and rock slides until the resting angle returns

questions.question: A hill made only of soft rock has:
options: No wall and no stands — no resistant band means no cliff, so the profile is just roof curving into pitch

questions.question: The shape chant for the four elements is:
options: Crest concave, cliff gentle, talus curved, pediment vertical
Crest straight, cliff concave, talus convex, pediment vertical
Crest convex, cliff vertical, talus straight, pediment concave

subtopics.title: The Walking Hill and the Chessboard Map

questions.question: Saying the stadium walks means that during slope retreat:
options: The wall is rebuilt further back, the stands follow, and the pitch stretches forward — the profile relocates without changing shape
The hill collapses into a round mound
The pediment moves up the hill

questions.question: After tens of millions of years of walking, the merged pitches form:
options: The PEDIPLAIN, with koppies and inselbergs standing as the last unconsumed remnants

questions.question: In the pins-and-string picture of vector data:
options: Every feature becomes a grid square
Pins are rivers and strings are farms
A PIN marks a point feature, STRING traces a line feature, a fenced patch encloses an area — each with its card of attributes

questions.question: Feeding a chessboard of heights — a digital elevation model — into a GIS lets it:
options: Calculate the STEEPNESS of every hillside in a district in seconds — the map conservation officers and engineers need
